criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask`: a test builds a temporary git repo and shows the printed fingerprint is unchanged by a records-only change and by an owner-path change, and changes after a governed change.
criteria.evidence: I ran the command. fingerprint_ignores_records_and_owner_paths and fingerprint_changes_with_governed_content passed. Each one builds a temporary repo with .gitattributes marking FRONT.md athena-exclude and SPEC.md athena-readonly, plus a records/ dir. It then runs the built xtask binary `fingerprint` and checks equality after the records-only and owner-path commits, and inequality after a src/ change.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask`: a test of the step script/workflow logic shows a missing entry or a failed run leads to the full job and no save, a hit of a passing entry skips the build and checks, and the save happens only after the checks pass.
criteria.evidence: All ci_cache_* tests passed. They cover: a missing or empty dir gives skip=false; a foreign or empty fingerprint gives skip=false; the outcomes failure, cancelled, skipped and empty write no marker and the next check is still a miss; success writes the marker, after which skip=true. In policy.rs, the_pass_is_marked_and_saved_only_after_the_checks... passed. It asserts the order checks < mark < save, that mark uses steps.checks.outcome, and that neither the save nor the mark step uses always(), failure() or cancelled().

criteria.criterion: .github/workflows/ci.yml keeps the job name 'fmt, clippy, tests'; the cache lookup (actions/cache/restore, key from the xtask fingerprint) comes before 'Set up'; setup, the checks and the existing cache steps are skipped on a hit; the new save step runs only when the checks succeeded.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff: the job name is unchanged. The order is Fingerprint, then actions/cache/restore with key steps.fingerprint.outputs.key, then gate, then report, then restores, setup and checks. Every step after the gate except the report has `if: steps.gate.outputs.skip != 'true'`. The save step has no status override, so it runs only if the earlier steps succeeded. The policy test the_checks_job_looks_up_its_earlier_pass_before_setup_and_skips_on_a_hit enforces this and passed.

criteria.criterion: Saving is done on pull-request branches for their own fingerprint entries, while the shared toolchain/registry/target caches are still saved only from the default branch; the entry is written under a key that includes the fingerprint and a marker whose presence means 'passed' (a failed run never writes one).
criteria.evidence: The diff shows 'Save the pass under the fingerprint' has no event or branch condition, and its key is ci-pass-<fingerprint without the sha256: prefix>. The three shared saves keep `github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == ...default_branch`. ci_cache.rs `mark` writes ci-pass/passed only when the outcome is success. The policy test asserts these conditions.

criteria.criterion: The hit step reports the reused result in the log and step summary (fingerprint and matched key), so a reader can see why the build was skipped.
criteria.evidence: The report step runs only when skip == 'true'. It passes FINGERPRINT and steps.ci-pass.outputs.cache-matched-key with --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY". report_text prints 'reused an earlier pass; setup, build and checks skipped' with the fingerprint and the matched key. ci_cache_report_names_the_fingerprint_and_the_matched_key checks that both stdout and the summary file contain them.

criteria.criterion: The fingerprint comes from athena-git's `fingerprint` (not a reimplementation); any dependency or architecture-doc change this needs keeps `dependency_direction_matches_the_architecture` passing.
criteria.evidence: ci_cache::fingerprint_command calls athena_git::attrs::fingerprint(&git, "HEAD", "HEAD"). cargo tree shows athena-git under xtask. The architecture.md row is now 'data, git', and dependency_direction_matches_the_architecture passed. Running the command on this tree printed a sha256 fingerprint.

findings.summary: New file xtask/src/ci_cache.rs is not on the expected deliverables list
findings.evidence: The deliverables list xtask/src/main.rs (modify) but not a new ci_cache.rs. The file holds the fingerprint and ci-cache logic, which the list placed in main.rs. It adds no scope beyond the request, and the planned demonstrations still run.

findings.summary: The pre-setup build uses the runner's `cargo +stable` while the workspace sets rust-version = 1.97; nothing verified on a real runner
findings.evidence: Cargo.toml sets rust-version = "1.97". If the runner image's stable is older than that, the fingerprint step fails and the job fails, with no fallback to the full run. D121 says a real workflow run was not measured. I estimate the runner's stable is newer than 1.97 by this date, but that is unmeasured.

findings.summary: A failed fingerprint step fails the job instead of falling back to the full run
findings.evidence: The Fingerprint step has no continue-on-error, and all later steps check steps.gate.outputs.skip. If xtask fails to build before setup, the whole job fails. That is safe (it never skips falsely) but less robust.

summary: The change does what was asked: the 'fmt, clippy, tests' job now skips setup and the checks when an earlier passing run had the same governed content, and runs everything otherwise. I ran `cargo test -p xtask --test fingerprint` (10 tests) and `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` (11 tests); all passed. They show the new `xtask fingerprint` command, which calls athena-git's own `attrs::fingerprint` on HEAD, ignores records-only and owner-path changes and changes when governed content changes. They also show that a missing or foreign cache entry, or a failed run, means the full job runs and nothing is saved, and that a saved pass means the next run skips. The ci.yml structure tests check the step order and conditions: the lookup comes before setup, the job name is unchanged, a pass is saved on pull-request branches too, and the three shared caches are still saved only from the default branch. The xtask to athena-git dependency is recorded in docs/architecture.md and the dependency-direction test passes. D121 and the CHANGELOG entry give the 15.4-minute median before, the alternatives, and say the after-figure is not yet measured. I could not check the 15.4 figure, because the job records are absent from this snapshot. Athena's fmt, clippy and test checks passed. I found no blocker or major issues. Minor: the new file xtask/src/ci_cache.rs was not on the deliverables list. Also, the pre-setup build relies on the runner's stable Rust being at least 1.97, and no real workflow run has tested that.
